title: Compact trace annotation and causal latency map
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This document describes the Compact Trace Annotation (CTA) format and the downstream Causal Latency Map (CLM) workflow we use to convert sparse, high-throughput traces into actionable latency attribution for inference requests. CTA+CLM provide a low-overhead instrumentation pattern suitable for production GPU pools and multi-tenant serving, enabling root-cause identification for P95/P99 regressions without capturing full trace payloads.

Why this exists
----------------
- Full-span tracing is too heavy for production inference: memory, disk, and network overheads degrade throughput and interfere with kernel scheduling.
- We need deterministic, reproducible attributions: whether latency comes from kernel contention, queueing, inter-node NVLink transfer, or KV cache misses.
- On-call and SRE teams require a compact artifact that can be stored for weeks and replayed into investigation tools.

Scope
-----
This doc covers:
- CTA schema (telemetry fields included and required)
- Collector configuration and rate controls
- CLI and pipeline to generate the CLM (processing and causal inference steps)
- Investigation runbook tied to SLO thresholds and alerts
- Dashboard and alert configuration snippets

Audience
--------
Primary: eng-serving-runtime, eng-sre, profiling engineers, incident responders. Secondary: product reliability, platform owners.

Telemetry contract: Compact Trace fields
-------------------------------------
We intentionally limit fields to keep artifacts small (~1–4KB per trace). Required fields are bold. Optional fields are encouraged when available. Keep field types primitive (string/number/boolean) to simplify downstream processing.

| Field | Type | Required? | Description |
|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
| request_id | string | yes | Global request identifier (UUID v4).
| ts_start | int | yes | Epoch ms when request first arrived at entry router.
| ts_end | int | yes | Epoch ms when response sent to client.
| stage_events | list<string> | yes | Ordered small tokens representing stage boundaries; see allowed tokens below.
| kernel_slots | list<int> | no | Compact histogram of per-kernel execution duration buckets (ms). Format: [count_lt1ms, count_1_5ms, count_5_10ms, count_gt10ms].
| kvcache_hits | int | no | Number of KV cache hits during request.
| kvcache_misses | int | no | Number of KV cache misses during request.
| shard_id | string | yes | Shard or node id handling primary compute for request.
| tenant | string | yes | Customer/tenant id (for multi-tenant pool attribution).
| kernel_hint | string | no | Optional model kernel hint (e.g. "fused-attn-v2", "triton-gemm").
| sampling_reason | string | yes | "p95-sample", "error-sample", "system-sample", "random".
| trace_version | string | yes | e.g. "cta-v1"

Allowed stage_events tokens (alphabetical): ENTRY, ENQUEUE, DEQUEUE, KERNEL_START, KERNEL_END, KV_LOOKUP_START, KV_LOOKUP_END, NETWORK_TX_START, NETWORK_TX_END, FALLBACK_SWITCH, RESPONSE_SEND

Compact Trace example (CTA payload)
----------------------------------
Example CTA (JSON single-line):
{"request_id":"b6f3c2d4-8e9f-4a2b-9cde-aa11bb22cc33","ts_start":1700000123456,"ts_end":1700000123590,"stage_events":["ENTRY","ENQUEUE","DEQUEUE","KERNEL_START","KERNEL_END","RESPONSE_SEND"],"kernel_slots":[0,1,0,0],"kvcache_hits":2,"kvcache_misses":0,"shard_id":"shard-eu-12","tenant":"acct-42","sampling_reason":"p95-sample","trace_version":"cta-v1"}

Collector configuration and rate controls
---------------------------------------
- Service name: inference-trace-collector (k8s: infra/observability).
- Default retention: compact traces stored in hot-s3 (14d), cold-s3 (90d).
- Sampling policy (k8s ConfigMap):
  1) p95-sampler: deterministic capture of requests where request_latency > 95th percentile (computed via streaming aggregator), priority 1.
  2) error-sampler: capture on any 5xx or model-runtime exception, priority 0 (always capture).
  3) system-sampler: capture 0.05% random traffic for long-term health signal, priority 2.
- Backpressure: if collector ingestion queue > 75% capacity, reduce system-sampler to 0.01% and drop random-samples older than 10s. Always preserve error-sampled traces.

Collector Config snippet (YAML)
-----------------------------
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cta-collector-config
data:
  sampling.p95.threshold-ms: "200"
  sampling.system.rate-per-minute: "50"
  retention.hot-days: "14"
  retention.cold-days: "90"
  ingestion.queue-soft-limit: "0.75"

Processing pipeline to build the Causal Latency Map (CLM)
------------------------------------------------------
High-level steps:
1) Ingest CTA artifacts from hot-s3 for window W (typically last 6h).
2) Enrich each CTA with node-level kernel telemetry (kernel queue lengths, kernel dispatch times) from the kernel-metrics store (TSDB).
3) Group traces by shard_id + tenant + model_variant.
4) Build causal graph using stage_events ordering and per-stage timestamps: compute edge weights for queueing delay, kernel duration, network transfer, and kvcache penalty.
5) Aggregate graphs into a CLM that reports per-path contributions to request latency percentiles.

Command-line helpers (example)
-----------------------------
# Pull CTAs into local file for window 1h
redwoodctl trace fetch --from now-1h --to now --out ctas.ndjson --filter sampling_reason=p95-sample

# Enrich and build CLM
redwoodctl trace enrich --ctas ctas.ndjson --kernel-store tsdb://kernel-metrics --out enriched.ndjson
redwoodctl clm build --in enriched.ndjson --group-by shard_id,tenant,model_variant --out clm-20260218.json

Interpretation semantics
------------------------
- Edge weights are additive: total request latency ~= sum(edge weights on primary path) + residual.
- An edge labeled KERNEL_QUEUE indicates time spent waiting for kernel slot; KERNEL_EXEC indicates execution time.
- KV cache penalty: modeled as (miss_count * avg_kv_lookup_ms) + miss-induced-kernel-delay.

Investigation runbook (p95 alert)
--------------------------------
Trigger: alert runtime-p95-slo-violation firing (SLO: p95 < 180ms for hosted small).
1) Page on-call (primary SRE) and create incident in our tracker.
2) Run quick CLI to sample CTAs for the impacted window:
   redwoodctl trace fetch --from now-30m --to now --filter sampling_reason=p95-sample --out incident-ctas.ndjson
3) Run fast CLM build limited to tenant(s) in alert:
   redwoodctl trace enrich --ctas incident-ctas.ndjson --kernel-store tsdb://kernel-metrics --out incident-enriched.ndjson
   redwoodctl clm build --in incident-enriched.ndjson --group-by shard_id,tenant --out incident-clm.json --top-paths 10
4) Inspect incident-clm.json for primary contributors: queueing, kernel_exec, kv_miss, network.
5) If root cause is kernel contention on shard X:
   a) Check shard-level kernel queue length: grafana -> Kernel Dispatch -> shard X.
   b) If queue length > 5 for > 5m, consider immediate temporary mitigation: scale out shard pool or reroute low-priority tenants.
6) If root cause is KV cache misses:
   a) Confirm model variant and session affinity changes.
   b) Trigger KV cache prefetch for affected sessions (see KV prefetch playbook).
7) If root cause is network/NVLink transfer: verify network device errors and open infra incident.
8) Document findings on incident page and attach CLM artifact.

Escalation thresholds and ownership
----------------------------------
- SRE responder: pager duty -> eng-sre oncall.
- If CLM shows >40% contribution from kernel_queue across multiple shards for >10min, escalate to runtime-platform@redwood.com and CC oncall infra.
- If KV-miss contribution >30% for a tenant with reserved capacity, page the assigned solutions engineer.

Dashboards and alerts (suggested panels)
---------------------------------------
- CLM: stacked contribution chart (kernel_exec / kernel_queue / kv_penalty / network) per tenant.
- Kernel queue length heatmap by shard (alert if a shard has >5 queue length for 5m).
- CTA ingestion health: queue occupancy and dropped trace rate (alert if >1%).

Example Grafana alert (pseudo-YAML)
----------------------------------
alert: runtime-p95-slo-violation
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_variant)) > 0.18
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: critical
annotations:
  runbook: "/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook-2026"

Performance cost and storage sizing guidance
-------------------------------------------
- CTA size: 1–4KB typical. Expect ~0.5GB/day per 10k p95-sampled requests at default sampling.
- Hot-s3 retention cost: plan for 14 days hot retention unless investigating large incidents; cold retention for months only on a per-need basis.
- CPU cost: enrichment step is CPU-heavy (TSDB lookups + graph building). For 1M CTAs, allocate at least 32 vCPU and 128GB RAM for the batch job.

Rollout checklist (safe deployment)
----------------------------------
1) Deploy collector config to staging with sampling p95 threshold at 2x current production baseline.
2) Validate CTA size and ingestion queue with canary traffic.
3) Run enrichment pipeline on staging CTAs and validate CLM graphs match synthetic ground truth.
4) Gradually reduce p95 threshold and move config to prod. Monitor ingestion queue and kernel-metrics tsdb latency.

Appendix: compact trace to full-trace mapping policy
---------------------------------------------------
- When on-call requires deep dive beyond CTA, create a short window full-span capture for the affected shard and tenant (max 100 requests, TTL 24h). Follow the full-trace capture playbook to avoid high production impact.
- Use CTA as first-line triage; full traces only for confirmed complex incidents.

Appendix: sample clm JSON (trimmed)
-----------------------------------
{"clm_window":"2026-02-18T14:00:00Z/2026-02-18T15:00:00Z","top_paths":[{"path":"ENTRY->ENQUEUE->DEQUEUE->KERNEL_QUEUE->KERNEL_EXEC->RESPONSE","p95_contrib_ms":45,"p95_share_pct":56,"example_request_ids":["b6f3c2d4-8e9f-4a2b-9cde-aa11bb22cc33"]}],"aggregate":{"kernel_exec_ms":40,"kernel_queue_ms":30,"kv_penalty_ms":5}}
